extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, regulatory officials and National Assembly staff in Korea (and advisers on regulatory reform)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for regulatory review, stakeholder engagement, RIA/CICO use, programmed review mechanisms, compliance/inspection and legislative quality checks aimed at improving regulatory quality in Korea. Includes international examples and practical recommendations for institutions and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Could a feasible alteration be made to the regulation to spur new markets, technologies, or jobs?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment question asking whether regulatory changes could stimulate markets, technologies or employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as part of regulatory review to identify if revisions can generate positive economic/innovation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have new or less costly methods, technologies, and/or innovative techniques emerged since this regulation was finalised?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether new or cheaper methods/technologies now allow regulated entities to achieve intended environmental (or other) results more effectively/efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider technical/market developments since finalisation that may warrant regulatory revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the regulation could include greater flexibilities for the regulated community to encourage innovative thinking and identify the least costly methods for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design rules to allow alternative compliance routes and lower-cost solutions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and technological objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether advances in risk assessment science or changes in underlying scientific data support updated evaluations of the regulation’s impacts (including on vulnerable groups such as environmental justice communities, children or the elderly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update impact assessments and evidence bases when scientific knowledge has advanced or new data become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request submission of RIA and CICO to the National Assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Request the executive branch to submit all relevant scrutiny materials such as RIAS and Cost-in, Cost-out (CICO) analyses to the National Assembly so parliament can consider regulatory impacts when reviewing or drafting bills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement by streamlining documentation and providing essential, succinct, salient and timely information to the Assembly for debate and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand and improve the CICO system
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand the CICO system to be as all-encompassing as possible and establish targets when reducing regulations through the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand metrics used in CICO to include measures such as public safety or other social costs and set targets (e.g., regulatory cost impact on the overall budget) to guide cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring indirect costs (Germany example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs (incidental to the main purpose of regulations) such as impacts on prices and general price level should be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include: ministry fills out a checklist for better regulations; follow a guide with practical examples; collect data from the Federal Statistical Office; where no data exists, consult businesses/associations early via inquiries and consultations; use cost estimates, cost-effectiveness analysis or cost–benefit analysis; and where quantification is impossible use qualitative forecasts. Indirect costs should be included when measuring cost impacts to ensure regulations do not hamper development or income opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empower actors at all levels and set clear KPIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Empower actors and responsible authorities by re-integrating/streamlining procedures, setting clear goals, and introducing meaningful definitions of key performance indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider establishing or empowering an independent think-tank to advise government on RIA and provide capacity-building and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a permanent legislative quality check mechanism for the National Assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish permanent structures or mechanisms within the National Assembly to provide independent technical advice on costs and benefits of legislation and to monitor regulatory quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include: (i) an RRC-like body mixing technical experts and business/labour reps; (ii) strengthen National Assembly Budget Office and Research Service roles; (iii) provide members access to a common budget for analysis; (iv) require parliament-initiated proposals to be accompanied by an impact assessment/CBA via CICO; (v) automatic sunset clauses for measures passed without RIA; (vi) require ex post evaluation after an allotted period; (vii) establish a permanent monitoring body for regulatory outcomes, processes and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunsetting (programmed review mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic annulment of a statutory act after a certain period (typically five to ten years) unless retention is explicitly justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be effective, exemptions and deferrals must be limited and re-made regulations require appropriate assessment; requires systematic preparation and planning and is often implemented together with regulatory clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process failure post-implementation review (PIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex post evaluation performed on regulations that should have required ex ante impact assessment, to re-assess regulations made in haste or without sufficient assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as a 'fail-safe' to catch potentially harmful regulations before they have been in place too long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex post review requirements in new regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: New regulations should outline how they will be subsequently evaluated (ex post review) often determined during RIA preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly useful where there are significant uncertainties or transitional elements; may not provide a full review but helps manage uncertain impacts and controversial changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement and transparency (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder engagement improves transparency in the regulatory procedure but requires emphasis on representation and ease of access; current systems have limited involvement from SMEs, start-ups, labour and foreign enterprises at early design phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve access (language, process translation), broaden representation, and use portals like Regulatory Information Portal and Regulatory Reform Sinmungo to increase engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Reform Sinmungo procedural timelines and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sinmungo platform accepts petitions on regulatory inconveniences; responsible officials must accept or decline within 14 days, justify refusals within three months (one month for urgent cases rejected but deemed reasonable by RRO) and provide feedback within one week for urgent petitions; reviewer information is revealed throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If refusal rationale is insufficient, the RRC can issue recommendations to the responsible agency. The system is complaint-driven and needs mechanisms for broader/systematic review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Information Portal design principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Central platform for public engagement in regulatory reform; personal information is not collected to encourage participation; agencies are encouraged to reflect public/business suggestions in proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If stakeholder engagement is insufficient (notably in RIA), agencies should revise the RIA statement. Portal should provide information on regulations and advertise successful regulatory reform cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance consultations to improve legislative drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations should engage relevant stakeholders (including local administration) early and ensure adequate representation to help co-design legislation and contribute real-life expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement of a wide range of stakeholders (local authorities, SMEs, labour, new entrants and incumbents) can improve draft quality and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support capacity within public administration to engage stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Build capacity for modern engagement methods, including social media and behavioural insights, and provide training/support for public officials responsible for engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accompany training with incentives for application in day-to-day activities (e.g., incorporate into performance appraisal systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define clear accountability rules for engagement processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and communicate who is responsible for what in engagement processes to manage stakeholder expectations and avoid unfair criticism of officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with principle-based rules (e.g., duty for officials to reasonably consider representations within a certain timeframe) and communicate general outcomes rather than individual case-by-case communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation criterion 1: When to consult (UK Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal consultations should take place at a stage when there is scope to influence the policy outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult at a meaningful time to allow input to affect the final policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation criterion 2: Duration of consultation exercises (UK Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation should normally last for at least 12 weeks with consideration for longer timescales where feasible and sensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow sufficient time for considered responses, especially for significant or complex proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation criterion 3: Clarity of scope and impact (UK Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation documents should be clear about the consultation process, what is being proposed, the scope to influence and the expected costs of the proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make documents understandable and explicit about impact and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation criterion 4: Accessibility and consultation exercises (UK Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation exercises should be designed to be accessible to, and clearly targeted at, those people the exercise is intended to reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use methods and channels appropriate to target audiences to maximise participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation criterion 5: The burden of consultation (UK Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping the burden of consultation to a minimum is essential if consultations are to be effective and if consultees’ buy-in to the process is to be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary complexity or demands on consultees to reduce 'consultation fatigue'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation criterion 6: Responsiveness of consultation exercises (UK Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation responses should be analysed carefully and clear feedback should be provided to participants following the consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide feedback on how responses were used; demonstrate responsiveness to input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation criterion 7: Capacity to consult (UK Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials running consultations should seek guidance in how to run an effective consultation exercise and share what they have learned from the experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build and share institutional knowledge on effective consultation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and centralise better.go.kr as the central information portal
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to develop better.go.kr as the central portal for data, documentation and feedback on proposed regulation, linking other platforms to avoid duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote cross-institutional data sharing to reduce burden on applicants and improve quality of benchmarking and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review stakeholder engagement initiatives for effectiveness and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess existing stakeholder engagement initiatives to understand which are effective for the cost and time associated, enhancing those that work and reducing duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on initiatives that deliver value for both consumers and businesses and move engagement from 'listening' to proactive dialogue with shared responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalise stakeholder engagement standards in the National Assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop methods and formalised standards/requirements for stakeholder engagement in National Assembly rule-making, especially for laws initiated by Members of the National Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current National Assembly Act allows omission of procedural requirements; recommend officialised standards to align parliamentary practice with government-wide regulatory reform efforts (including RIA requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-ordination mechanisms for social media use across governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate social media practices and communities of practice across government to share good practices and engage stakeholders (examples: Denmark Open Government Camp, France SIG seminars, Netherlands 'Civil Servant 2.0', US GSA Social Media Community of Practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use regular meetings, seminars, and communities to spread good practices and improve citizen services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider delivery arrangements for regulatory enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory delivery can be carried out by government or delegated to other providers (central agencies, local governments, legally entrusted non-government bodies such as agencies or associations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When delegating to local governments, consider options: (1) regional government enforces directly; (2) regional enforces via sub-regional; (3) sub-regional enforces directly. Tailor arrangements to local needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of market-based compliance measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory compliance should consider both conventional command-and-control measures and market-based measures (self-regulation, voluntary agreements, economic inducement, release/disclosure of information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt market-based approaches where appropriate to encourage voluntary compliance and reduce burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory compliance survey metrics (RRO guideline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure regulatory awareness, recognition and conformity using specified sub-dimensions: awareness level (awareness, comprehension, clarity); recognition level (necessity, adequacy, fitness for purpose); conformity level (conformity, enforcement, adequacy of penalty imposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the guideline as a handbook for conducting compliance surveys and track these metrics annually to monitor regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate inspection and enforcement strategy into overall regulatory strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspection should be an integrated part of the overall regulatory strategy to ensure quality, effectiveness, and to complement compliance efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop coordinated inspection strategies, avoid ad hoc short-lived mechanisms, and plan strategically across political cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve and coordinate local governments in regulatory reform and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Local governments should be engaged in development of regulations and regulatory reform and have tailored regulations for local contexts; co-ordination across regional and sub-regional governments needs strengthening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use central government outreach and co-ordination to leverage local authorities' frontline experience and reduce confusion over roles, rights and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure adequate resources and skills for enforcement agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Address shortages in manpower and skills for enforcement agencies (e.g., occupational safety) to improve regulatory delivery; Korea's public sector employment in enforcement may lag other OECD countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase capacities proportionally with reform intensity, and target recruitment and training to critical enforcement areas.
